news.2026-10-28-ouganda-quarantaine-reto: Uganda imposes 21 days of quarantine, paid by travellers, on people coming back from DR Congo

The Health Ministry tightened the rules on 25 October: travellers who have been in Congo can no longer transit through the country. Two patients who passed through Entebbe airport tested positive in Kenya and Nigeria.
On 25 October, Uganda's Health Ministry announced that citizens returning from DR Congo must spend 21 days in quarantine, at their own expense [1][2].
Travellers who have stayed in Congo can no longer transit through Uganda, including on chartered flights [1].

Uganda has recorded no confirmed case since it declared its outbreak over on 28 July, but two people who passed through the country later tested positive, in Kenya and Nigeria; according to Africa CDC, both went through Entebbe airport on 3 October [1][2].
Key point: a country with no patients can still shut its door, because the virus travels with passengers [1][2].

The outbreak in DR Congo has killed thousands of people, and Uganda prefers to pay the price of caution (slower travel, transit ban) rather than reopen a hotspot at home [1]. Investigations into the case detected in Nigeria are still ongoing [1].
If you are planning a trip to East Africa, a stopover in Entebbe may be refused or complicated for anyone who has stayed in Congo: check the rules before you leave [1].

news.2026-10-28-hongrie-bloque-moldavie-: Hungary is still blocking the last two steps of Moldova's and Ukraine's path into the EU
After letting two negotiating chapters through on 13 October, Budapest refused on 20 October to open the last two, and its block was restated on the 27th.
On 13 October, in Luxembourg, the Union unblocked two more negotiating groups for Ukraine and Moldova [1].
On 20 October, Hungary again refused to approve the opening of the last two “chapters” out of six, with no explanation given, according to the Ukrainian press [1][2].
The block was restated on 27 October; the European Commission is due to present its enlargement roadmaps for Ukraine and Moldova on 4 November [3].
Key point: EU accession is decided chapter by chapter, and it only takes one country saying no to block a step [1][2].
In early October, the Brussels press wrote that Budapest might lift its block if Kyiv passed a law on minority schools, but that the veto in principle on membership itself remained in place [4].
Nothing changes for you right away. But each chapter opened brings two countries closer to the European market, and the sources give no entry date [1][3].

news.2026-10-28-fmi-moyen-orient-recul-o: War is shrinking the Middle East's economy by 1.3% in 2026: in the Gulf, only Oman escapes
In its October forecasts, the IMF sees the Middle East, North Africa and Pakistan region contracting this year, before a rebound in 2027.
The IMF expects the economy of the Middle East, North Africa and Pakistan region to shrink by 1.3% in 2026, after growth of 3.3% in 2025, then rebound by 6.6% in 2027 [1][2].
It blames the fall on the war's effects on energy production, shipping, tourism, trade and confidence [2][3].
Gulf (GCC) economies are all expected to contract in 2026, except Oman; according to the wire report carried by Polity, oil exporters are hit harder than importers [1][3].
Key point: the region that sells the world's energy is the one shrinking, because the war hits exactly energy, ships and tourists [2][3].
The IMF warns that a prolonged war, or new cuts to production, shipping routes or infrastructure, could make the picture worse [2].
When the oil and gas region suffers, energy stays expensive and fragile, which can weigh on your fuel and heating budget [1][2].

news.2026-10-28-philippines-ministres-de: In the Philippines, India and Japan send their defence ministers to a major regional meeting
On 28 and 29 October, Cebu hosts the meeting of ASEAN defence ministers and their partners, chaired this year by Manila.
The 13th meeting of ASEAN defence ministers and their partners (ADMM-Plus) takes place on 28 and 29 October in Cebu; the Philippines chairs it in 2026 [1][2].
India's Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has left for Cebu to “explore new avenues to strengthen strategic partnerships” [1][3].
Japan's Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi is expected from 28 October, with bilateral talks planned with his US, Philippine and South Korean counterparts [4].
Key point: these meetings are mostly about talking and building defence partnerships before a crisis breaks out [1][3].
The fact that India and Japan make the trip shows they want a say in Southeast Asia's security, a region many commercial ships pass through [1][4].
The security of Asian seas indirectly affects what you buy (electronics, clothing), which travels largely by ship: that is why these meetings matter even when nothing is signed.

news.2026-10-28-iran-poutine-moscou-somm: Iran's president in Moscow for a gas exporters' summit and a one-on-one with Putin
Masoud Pezeshkian was due to meet Vladimir Putin on 27 October, on the sidelines of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum summit. At the time of writing, no account of the meeting was available.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian was due to attend the 8th summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) in Moscow on 27 October, devoted to gas markets and cooperation among exporters [1][2].
According to Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, he was due to meet Vladimir Putin there; economic cooperation and “geopolitical” issues were on the agenda [2][3].
The two men had already met in Bishkek in early September: Pezeshkian then thanked Putin for Russia's stance during the war with the United States [4].
Key point: two major energy producers are talking just as the war disrupts Gulf gas and oil [2][4].
At the time of writing, no account of the meeting was available: this story is one to follow, and it is not yet known whether it will lead to an agreement.
The energy prices you pay depend partly on these producers: watch whether this meeting leads to anything concrete.

news.2026-10-28-nigeria-aide-transport-s: In Nigeria, the state avoids a showdown with the unions: 70,000 naira of transport aid for six months
The government and the NLC labour federation reached a deal on 27 October, but not on the date of a new minimum wage.

On 27 October, at a conciliation meeting at the Labour Ministry, the federal government approved a 70,000-naira transport allowance for workers at all levels, for six months starting in November 2026 [1].
Payment of allowance arrears, effective 1 May 2026, is also approved, in instalments starting in November; a deal also covers 19 months of arrears for health workers [1][2].

The two sides did not agree on when a new minimum wage should take effect [1]. On 9 October, the union had given the government two weeks to cut petrol prices and reopen negotiations on the minimum wage [3].
Key point: the government answers anger over the cost of living with temporary aid rather than a lasting rise in the minimum wage [1][3].

The union says inflation and transport costs have eroded the value of the current 70,000-naira minimum wage; a senior Labour Ministry official said a new minimum wage was under discussion, with no negotiation date set [3].
It is the same mechanism as here when fuel prices rise: workers who pay for their commute see their purchasing power melt, and the state chooses between helping out or raising wages.

news.2026-10-28-perou-or-illegal-tambopa: Tambopata Reserve, Madre de Dios, Peru
In Peru, the authorities destroy dozens of illegal gold camps in the Amazon, but the miners come back
More than 30 illegal gold-mining camps near the Tambopata reserve have been destroyed, according to the Latin American business press.
Peruvian authorities have destroyed more than 30 illegal gold-mining camps near the Tambopata National Reserve, in the Amazon [1].
In August, an operation led by prosecutors, with support from the US non-profit Global Conservation, had already destroyed nearly 1.7 million dollars' worth of mining equipment in the reserve [2].
A prosecutor quoted by the press admits that “mining is winning”: miners return within days of each raid [2].
Key point: destroying camps is not enough as long as illegal gold pays far more than the risk costs [1][2].

According to a report cited by the press, Peru's illegal gold exports may have reached about 11.5 billion dollars in 2025, and frequent changes of president have prevented a sustained strategy against this trade [2].
The gold in your jewellery or investments comes partly from mines whose origin is hard to check: that is why gold traceability is becoming an issue.
